about: Prompts kept in agents/prompts.md, chosen by the architect's criteria: how the agents were directed (instructions, formats, conventions, duplicate rules, structure, tokens). Keys are <session>@<timestamp> from the Claude Code transcripts. Architect prompts after reviewed_until are not classified yet; export_prompts.py lists them.

themes.title: Requirements and knowledge base
themes.summary: Pinning the docs to 1.5.6, a rule inventory per Area, and a local RAG index, with questions on how retrieval is scoped and kept current.

themes.title: Test case format and design rules
themes.summary: The seed formats, Areas, the Review field, how open questions are written into cases, where each technique applies, cross-functional scope and data-driven cases.

themes.title: Agent instructions: writing and refining them
themes.summary: Creating each agent, then tightening its instructions from what went wrong: guardrails, an assertion for every filled field (and no checks on untouched fields or unasked absences), never inferring the opposite of a rule, missed negative cases, generator traces.

themes.title: Duplicate detection and independent review
themes.summary: A scored duplicate checker, an LLM judge for borderline scores, merging the judge into a full reviewer, rule coverage checks and the log of what the reviewer caught.

themes.title: Orchestration and running the agents
themes.summary: From starting agents by hand to one skill per stage, many cases per run, unattended headless runs, and prompts that name only the functionality.

themes.title: Automation framework and conventions
themes.summary: The layered Playwright framework, real-form login (only as the test's own user, with no all-users login step), one config for UI and API, environments, and schema checks that report without hiding the other checks.

themes.title: Tokens, cost and speed
themes.summary: Cutting what the agents read and run: a heading index, Area-wise inventories, agent file size, prompt caching, skipping login runs, smaller page snapshots.

themes.title: Verification against the app and approval
themes.summary: Running cases through Playwright MCP and the API before approving them, automating only Approved cases, and turning a wrong assumption into a finding.

themes.title: Project structure and deliverables
themes.summary: CLAUDE.md, folder naming, one automation project, the submission documents, and keeping the case folders tidy.
